title: Sycamore Knoll undersea base claim rejected
place_text: Sycamore Knoll, off Point Dume, Southern California

tellings.quote: There was no alien base there.
we did the research and we're like I don't think there's anything
tellings.difference: Michels describes his own research with Will O'Brien into a rover survey, rather than Gallaudet's assessment.
tellings.link_reason: Like telling 1, it dismisses the Point Dume undersea base claim, here based on Michels and Will O'Brien's own look at the rover survey.

as_told.title: Michels and Will O'Brien look into a rover survey at Point Dume

related.note: Both concern the claimed alien base off Point Dume (Sycamore Knoll); the story asserts a base that was erased from maps, while this telling says there was no base.

plain: There is a claim that aliens keep a base under the sea at Sycamore Knoll, an underwater hill off Point Dume on the Southern California coast, and on this podcast it is turned down. Tim Gallaudet, a retired Navy admiral, says it plainly: "There was no alien base there." He mentions the idea as it appears in the book Undersea UFO Base by a writer named Preston Dennett. Michels says he looked into it himself with a man named Will O'Brien, going through a survey made by an underwater rover. "We did the research and we're like I don't think there's anything," he says. Both tell it to set aside this one spot, even as they discuss unexplained things in the ocean.
